Trigger_Condition: list->capacity reaches 2^63 items on 64-bit ABI and triggers growth
Unsafe_State: new_cap wraps around to 0 or smaller value modulo 2^64
Possible_Consequence: Heap allocation of 0 bytes, leading to subsequent heap buffer overflow
Existing_Guards: None explicitly in product.c before multiplication (relies implicitly on system RAM limits)
Notes: Arithmetically satisfiable if capacity unbounded; unreachable in practice on 64-bit due to RAM exhaustion before 2^63 items.

Trigger_Condition: new_cap exceeds 8.86e16 items, causing multiplication overflow
Unsafe_State: Multiplication wraps around, realloc allocates smaller buffer than required

Existing_Guards: None explicitly checking new_cap <= SIZE_MAX / sizeof(Product) in product.c
Suggested_Verification_Method: SMT Bit-Vector Solver (Z3) / CBMC Bounded Model Checker
Notes: Critical formal verification target. On 32-bit systems, SIZE_MAX/208 = 20,647,663 items which is reachable.

Memory_Object: Borrowed pointer Product* to element inside dynamic array list->items
Preconditions: Caller holds borrowed pointer returned by find_product*() and subsequently calls add_product()
Trigger_Condition: add_product triggers realloc() which moves array to new heap address
Unsafe_State: Held pointer points to freed old heap memory (Dangling Pointer)
Possible_Consequence: Use-after-free read or write when dereferencing old pointer
Existing_Guards: No language-level borrow checker. Current v0 baseline callers in main.c do NOT hold pointers across add_product
Suggested_Verification_Method: CBMC Pointer Invariant Check / ASan Simulation Harness
Notes: Architectural contract hazard. Safe in current main.c execution, but unsafe API contract for composition.
